text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH

- President Suleyman Demirel has said the petition signed by MPs, vowing not to support a government formed by opposition parties, is unconstitutional since deputies should vote with their conscience and not be bound before a parliamentary debate.
- Ministries run by the Islam-based Welfare Party are rushing to complete tenders worth many billions of lira in the expectation they will soon be out of power.
MILLIYET

- Demirel refused to be drawn into the row on whether he should have given deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller the chance to form a government, but has told opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz to continue his quest to build a secularist coalition.
- Left-wing leader Deniz Baykal told a conference his party was no longer in favour of collective state ownership in the economy.
HURRIYET
- Secularist Yilmaz has agreed with opposition leaders on the distribution of cabinet seats in an anti-Islamist coalition.
- Turkey's largest industrial conglomerate, Koc Holding, has reached a settlement with the Ford Motor Company to equalise their shares in the Turkey-based automotive producer Otosan.
YENI YUZYIL
- The military-dominated National Security Council has demanded legislation to bring under control the growing number of religious foundations.
- Generous wage increases to civil servants before a general election will cost the country dearly.
RADIKAL

- All eyes are on 33 MPs from Ciller's True Path Party who are said to be unhappy with the partnership with Necmettin Erbakan's Islamists. Yilmaz will need their votes to stand a chance of forming an anti-Islamist alliance government.
- The manager of a factory making ethylene has said the Islamist local authority closed the plant down, thinking the alcohol was for human consumption.
CUMHURIYET
- More resignations and defections from Ciller's True Path and Erbakan's Welfare Party are expected in the next few days.
ZAMAN
- Yilmaz and Ciller are fighting their most important battle to be undisputed champion of the right.
DUNYA
- The tender for the privatisation of state bank Etibank will have to be repeated since the company who bought the bank has not kept up with the payments for it.
